problem: VLMap-style semantic maps only encode category-level semantics, so they cannot distinguish different instances of the same object class or use attributes like color, and can only navigate to the nearest object of a category.
motivation: Real-world commands such as 'navigate to the fourth black chair across from the table' need instance index and attribute grounding. A map holding per-instance and per-attribute information would enable precise zero-shot LLM-driven navigation.
key_idea: Segment the bird's-eye-view reconstruction with SAM and assign each mask a category label and color label via region matching against the VLMap pixel-text similarity, producing an instance- and attribute-aware map that an LLM can query through code.
insight: Instance masks from SAM smooth noisy per-pixel VLM labels and give countable instances, enabling coarse-to-fine localization (mask lookup, then VLMap refinement). The gains over VLMap are modest (e.g. SR 0.54 to 0.64 in one scene), and evaluation is small-scale, so the evidence is limited. There is no ablation of the individual components.
method: BEV VLMap and 3D reconstruction: LSeg features are projected from RGB-D frames into a top-down grid, with a height matrix keeping only pixels below robot height.
SAM instance segmentation: SAM segments the BEV reconstruction map into masks, and each mask is stored with attributes such as area, bbox, label, label_id, num_of_same_class and color.

Region matching and label scoring: the pixel-label map is masked by each SAM mask, and unique-label counts are ratioed and sorted (top-k) to choose the mask's category; the same procedure with color text gives the color label.
LLM-generated category list: Llama2 turns a natural-language map request into the object category list fed to LSeg/CLIP text encoders.
Two-step landmark localization: coarse mask lookup in the instance (U) and color (V) maps, then fine localization in the VLMap.

LLM code generation for navigation: GPT or Llama-2-13b-chat (GPTQ 4-bit) parses commands into (object, index, color) and generates Python calls to a high-level function library (get_obj_attributes, move_to_left, face, etc.).
Interactive data collection: CMU-Exploration combined with Habitat for controllable RGB-D and pose collection, using about 8% less data than VLMap.

setting.backbone: LSeg + CLIP + SAM (frozen) with Llama-2-13b-chat (4-bit GPTQ) or ChatGPT for code generation

setting.action_space: high-level map-based functions (move_to, face, turn, move_forward), executed as low-level control

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks on hand-curated tasks in four Matterport3D scenes, not standard benchmarks; SR values in Table 1 are printed as fractions (0-1); T_4 is the task success rate.
results: IVLMap outperforms VLMap, CoW and CLIP Map on all four scenes, with subgoal SR of 0.48-0.67 against VLMap's 0.43-0.56. In zero-shot language-driven navigation, T_4 is 0.14 against 0.08 for VLMap. The abstract claims an average 14.4% improvement in navigation accuracy.
limitations: Small, hand-made evaluation (four scenes, 36 trajectories) with no standard benchmark, and only success rate is reported
Static, pre-built 2D BEV map cannot handle dynamic environments or object height; requires prior exploration with poses
No ablations of SAM, color attributes, or the LLM choice, and the real-robot results are only qualitative
